For Athanasius, Ambrose, Hilary, Augustine and the others such would never have composed so many and such magnificent treatises if the manifold error of the heretics had not arisen against the right faith. But while the heretics strove to build up a lie with the testimonies of the Scriptures, the fathers were compelled to refute them by the authority of the same Scriptures and to set forth how they are rightly to be understood. Hence we, reading their writings, receive as it were more watchful keepers at the gates and porches of the city and temple, as it were more abundant ministers for the office of the altar and of the Lord's victims; because by their discourses we are instructed for the keeping of faith and good action and for serving more intently in the sight of the divine majesty. This can also be taken mystically of the persecution of the gentiles, by which the Church was often shaken; which on the occasion of the martyrs seemed to be utterly destroyed, but, while they were crowned in secret, was built the better; and as miracles shone forth from them even after death, a greater people flocked to the confession of the faith, until the very summit of the worldly empire bent its neck to the yoke of Christ; so that the state of the holy city, that is, the Church, long attacked by kings and princes, was helped and spread by their earnestness; as the kings of the Chaldeans, who are interpreted 'fierce' or 'as demons', overthrew Jerusalem, but the kings of the Persians, who are interpreted 'tried', restore it with friendly provision and exalt it with due honour.
19_interl217: spiritual men, namely, taken up into the lot of the kingdom
19_interl218: because "the Son of man shall send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds"
19_marg276: BEDE. The city had long since been built, but it was not fitting that it should be dedicated before, the inhabitants being gathered, fit ministers had been appointed for the temple and keepers for the gates and porches. And the holy city, when made, is dedicated when, the number of the elect being fulfilled at the end of the world, the Church is brought universally into heaven to the vision of its Maker; to whose life, whenever we are lifted up with desires in this life, we rejoice as it were over the future dedication of our city. Hence too the dedication can be taken in two ways: meanwhile, namely, in the hope of those who desire and cleanse the eyes of the heart with which they may see God; then in the very reality of blessed men enjoying the divine vision in spiritual bodies among the angelic hosts.
19_interl220: rejoicing together, namely, in the receiving of eternal life, and giving thanks to him by whose gift they deserved [so the edition: 'incruerunt'] to enter that city
19_marg277: Cymbals, psalteries and harps can be understood as the bodies of the just, then immortal, in which they will render most sweet sounds to the Lord. In the present life too the Levites are gathered in Jerusalem when the faithful, kindled by the memory of the peace above, place in it the whole delight of their mind, and rejoice, if not yet by beholding, at least by desiring, over the eternal inheritance in heaven which they hope to receive, according to that: "Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just" etc. For they keep the dedication with song and thanksgiving when, rejoicing in the Lord, they accept whatever adversity or prosperity befalls; they keep it with cymbals, psalteries and harps when they make the pleasing sounds of their works ascend to the ears of God and kindle the hearts of their neighbours to his love etc.
19_marg278: That is, the imitators of those who strove to serve the Lord with devout and cheerful mind and to sing his word by preaching to others. Who make themselves villages round about Jerusalem when with lofty heart they dwell in the neighbourhood of the homeland above, saying: "But our conversation is in heaven." And they make the same villages in the plains around Jerusalem when, with heart enlarged toward God, they humble themselves the more, the more sweetly they touch the glory of loftiness by tasting it. All of whom are now gathered man by man to the heavenly homeland by the advances of their works, and in the very time of the dedication, that is, of everlasting reward, are united there together.
19_marg279: AND [THE PRIESTS] WERE PURIFIED etc. BEDE. A wholly just order, that the doctors who desire to purify the people should first be purified, should chastise the body and bring it into subjection, lest perhaps, preaching to others, they be found reprobate. And the priests and Levites were purified by prayers and offerings of victims and by abstaining from their wives. And they purified the people by preaching the same continence. They purified the gates and the wall by going round with trumpets and canticles of psalms, the people accompanying, and, the circuit being completed, by offering victims for the state of the citizens and the city. And now too those who preside over the Church, taken by the Lord into the spiritual ministry, the greater memory they bear of our dedication, which will be in our resurrection, the more they strive to purify and sanctify themselves and those committed to them, lest perhaps anyone not having a wedding garment be cast out of the common joy of the holy city and, bound hand and foot, be sent into the exterior darkness.
19_marg280: That is, of confession or praise; the more perfect doctors of the Church are those who go up upon the wall at the dedication of the city, because in the time of tribulation they are shown to have surpassed the general life of the Church by living more loftily. For of these it is said: "Upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen." Rightly therefore those who now preside over the walls of the Church as watchmen will then too stand above them in the glory of reward.
19_interl221: namely of Jews and gentiles praising God in the homeland above; which is also done daily in this life
19_marg281: Either [it signifies that] they purge the filth of sins from the Church in the present by living more correctly and correcting those who err, and in the future expel from the city of the Lord, that is, from entrance into the heavenly homeland, by judicial power those who would not be corrected; or the companies of those giving praise, going to the right hand, go up upon the wall to the gate of the dunghill when they proclaim worthy of praise those who remove all uncleanness from the Church by preaching, rebuking and excommunicating.
19_interl222: because the just, by living rightly, both hasten to eternal life in the present and will come to it in the future
19_marg282: In this life the sons of the priests sound with trumpets at the dedication of the city who by preaching kindle the hearts of their hearers to the memory of the heavenly homeland.
19_marg283: Because they do not lean on their own sense or desires, but, following in all things the life and teaching of the fathers and prophets, persist in the word of preaching.
19_marg284: Because in all that they do they have before their eyes the words of holy Scripture, by whose leading they may come to the entrance of eternal life, that they may be inebriated with the plenty of the house of God and the torrent of his pleasure, with whom is the fountain of life etc.
19_interl223: "strong of hand and desirable in aspect"
19_marg285: BEDE. When the city was being built it was said that those who built the gate of the fountain carried the measure of their work up to the steps that go down from the city of God. There, therefore, a going down of the steps from the city is named; here, when the city is dedicated, a going up. And as there too a struggle with the enemy was carried on, here, the enemy conquered, joy is celebrated; because the saints who are humbled in the present under the mighty hand of God will be exalted in the future; who now build the walls of the Church on earth of living stones, that is, of holy souls, in affliction and perils and many watchings, then, the building completed and raised to heaven, rejoicing go up to contemplate the brightness of God.
19_marg286: And over against them etc. Not, that is, with the opposition of distance, but with the meeting of harmony, by which the elect in this life kindle one another to the love of God, and in that life, rejoicing together more perfectly in their mutual blessedness, praise him without weariness; as the seraphim, crying one to another, celebrate together the holy Trinity with fellow exultation.
19_interl224: which is all the just, who are filled with the grace of the Creator and inhabited by him
19_marg287: BEDE. The sons of the priests go up above the house of David when preachers or martyrs, as now they surpass the general life of the just in the ministry of the word or the struggle of martyrdom, so then go before their general rewards with the gift of a loftier recompense. Whence: Because thou hast been faithful in a little, thou shalt have power over ten cities. For as many as each instructs to life by word or example, for so many will he then be more gloriously honoured in the receiving of life. The priests also come up to the water gate toward the east when those who in this life, as the hart panteth after the fountains of water, so desired to come and appear before the face of God, attain to the fulfilment of their desire and deserve to see the rising of the sun of justice without setting.
19_interl226: that one might stir up the other
19_interl227: namely the loftiness and the guarding of works
19_marg288: BEDE. It is long to discourse specially on each of the gates or towers; let it suffice to have said only this: that those who finished the gates, towers and wall of the city with great labour, hardship, hunger, cold and many watchings, the enemy unwearied and lying in wait resisting, then, the enemy repelled and confounded, walking through the gates, towers and buildings of the same city with canticles, hymns and psalteries, cymbals, harps and trumpets, rejoice in thanksgiving together with the masters of the work and of the law of God. Which there is no doubt is done also in the spiritual building, when, the time of the last retribution being at hand, as at the long-desired dedication of the city of God, the faithful will obtain eternal rewards for their works; when, like Nehemias, Esdras and the other priests and Levites, each bringing forward his workers, all the masters of the faithful peoples lead those whom they have gained for the Lord to the walls of the heavenly homeland. Then among other things Nehemias goes with the company of those giving praise even upon the tower of the furnaces, in whose building he had toiled before, when the masters of truth rejoice over the lofty rewards of those whom they taught. For if the oven-baked loaves, which are baked in secret, signify the inner devotion of the mind of the faithful, strengthened by the fire of charity, whence also they are commanded to be offered in sacrifice to the Lord, what is figured by the furnaces in which the same loaves are baked if not the hearts of those who always burn with the flame of inward love and are wont to bring forth the deeds or words of the virtues? Of which it is well said: God, whose fire is in Sion, and his furnace in Jerusalem. They themselves too say of themselves: Was not our heart burning within us etc. But the hearts of the reprobate burn with the fire of crimes; whence: They are all adulterers, their hearts are as an oven. The builders of the holy city therefore build among other things the tower of the furnaces when the doctors instruct the hearts of their hearers in faith and work, that they may be kindled to receive the greater gifts of the Spirit and to bring forth daily new dishes of the virtues for the joy of the people of God. And rejoicing and singing praise to the Lord they walk upon the tower of the furnaces on the day of the dedication of Jerusalem when in the time of the future retribution they rejoice together over the glory of those whom they taught. The furnaces then are the hearts of the elect, in which the charity of God is poured forth by the Holy Spirit, who is given to them. And the tower of the furnaces is the loftiness and guard by which the same hearts must always be fortified with circumspect caution and solicitude, lest they can be hurt by malignant spirits, lest the flame of the virtues can be bent or troubled by the wind of pride.
19_interl228: of hearts burning with the flame of the Holy Spirit
19_interl230: joined, namely, from both peoples in one melody of divine praise, or made of angels and men, because "men shall be equal to the angels of God"
19_marg289: AND THERE STOOD etc. BEDE. Having walked round the walls and gates of the city with the song of joy and the instruments of musicians, they return to the temple of the Lord, that, standing there too, they may render praise to the Lord with trumpets sounding together and, victims being offered, fulfil the vows of the dedication. And the house of the Lord, like the city of the Lord, signifies the very homeland of the future life, as the penitent [so the edition] Church too is called the house of God and city; but there is a difference, because they are said to have gone up the buildings of the city praising with canticles of thanks and instruments, but in the house of God to have praised standing and to have sung loud. For the elect go up the walls of the city which they made when they enter the joys of the homeland above which they deserved by working well. They made the distributed loftiness of gates, steps and buildings when, entering the house of the Father, they behold there the distance of many mansions according to divers merits. In this life the just go up in the city of the Lord with hymns of dedication when, gaping with their whole heart toward the memory of the future reward, they advance daily in good works, according to that: "In his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears." And: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way" etc. For so they hold the innocence of heart and work they have received as always to strive to grow to higher things. And they stand in the house of the Lord with praises who persevere unwearied in that very advance of works, according to that of Elias: "The Lord liveth, in whose sight I stand", that is, in fulfilling whose will I remain with untiring mind.
19_marg290: "Thou hast broken my bonds: I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise." "I will pay my vows to the Lord in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the presence of all his people: in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem." This is done when, the multitude of all the saints being gathered in the heavenly homeland, we offer those praises for which we groan in the present and which we thirst for with daily desire in thanksgiving.
19_interl231: namely of everlasting light, of which Zacharias: "And there shall be one day, which is known to the Lord, not day nor night", that is, removed from the custom of passing [days]
19_interl232: because each, received in his mansion, perseveres in the perpetual vision of the Creator and celebrates his praises with harmonious voice
19_marg291: BEDE. These things belong to the dedication of the holy city, namely the heavenly Jerusalem, in which God is king, who gladdens the citizens with his presence; great joy is had. Whence: "I bring you good tidings of great joy, that shall be to all the people"; to distinguish it, namely, from human joy, which is a small and passing joy and therefore to be little valued. This dedication can be understood as begun in this life in certain of the elect who, the eye of the heart being purified, contemplate in part the future joys of the Church, as Isaias, Ezechiel, Daniel and the other prophets, and the apostles who saw the Lord glorified on the mount; who, the higher they entered the heights of the city above, the more clearly they took care to sing the praises of the Lord and to sacrifice the greatest victims of good works.
19_marg292: Because in the time of the resurrection not only those who built the Church by preaching or by working strongly receive the fruit of their labour, but the weaker sharers of the same faith also rejoice in the same receiving of life: "For the Lord hath blessed the little ones with the great."
19_marg293: BEDE. While all rejoiced over the building and dedication of the city, care was earnestly taken that the worship of religion in it, which was to be carried out chiefly in the ceremonies through the teaching and offices of the priests, Levites, singers and porters, should be kept and should grow. Therefore vigorous men were appointed who should diligently gather into the treasury of Christ the money contributed by the people and keep it for the use of the ministries of the temple and altar; and should keep with careful attention the firstfruits of the crops and the tithes and the wine for the libations which were brought to the temple; that, namely, there being an abundant supply of the things which were to be offered to the Lord or on which the ministers of the Lord should live, they themselves might the more willingly remain in Jerusalem, by whom the people might be taught and sanctified. The Lord too ordained that they who preach the gospel should live by the gospel. But woe to the priests and ministers who delight to take from the people the expenses of their grade, but are proved to labour nothing for its salvation, to furnish nothing of holy guidance [so the edition: 'sacri ductus'] by living rightly, to sing nothing sweet of the sweetness of the heavenly kingdom by preaching, and not to open the doors of the city above but to shut them by acting perversely; by whose works the people does not rejoice in praising God but is afflicted. It is to be noted indeed that Juda, who in the building of the city spoke in despair: "The strength of the bearer of burdens is decayed, and the rubbish is very much" etc., had now already recovered strength of mind and body to carry out the earth which hindered the building of the wall which had fallen, and to overcome the snares of the enemies which threatened. Rightly therefore he rejoices in the priests and Levites, singers and porters, by whose labour and exhortation he escaped the danger of so great an affliction and found the glory of so great prosperity. And thou therefore, if thou seest thy heart weighed down with the earth of vices, so that thou art not able to build in it a city worthy of the divine dwelling, if thou seest the malignant enemy drawing thee back from purging the rubbish of vices and from building the walls of the virtues, hear the consolation and counsels of the priests and the reading of the divine Scriptures; for so, the snares of the demons being driven out, God the victor enters the dwelling of thy breast as his city, to sanctify it and make his abode with thee.
19_marg294: For this reason he wished the priests and Levites and the other ministers of the saints to dwell in Jerusalem among the peoples, that [Juda] might rejoice in the good works of those by whose earnestness the people was corrected and the city built, and dedicated with great praise and joy.
19_interl233: that "they who preach the gospel should live by the gospel"
19_interl234: they gave tithes as to the saints of God
19_interl235: as offering to the greater the tenth part of their tithes
19_interl236: unless, namely, they cease to be such
19_marg295: AND ON THAT DAY etc. These, because they were born of incest, express the heretics, whose authors, when by understanding it ill they corrupt the teaching of the fathers in which they were instructed, use the father's seed like the daughters of Lot, by stealth and in darkness and not lawfully. And therefore their offspring, that is, their followers, can never have a part in the Church of God. For if any are corrected, they are no longer sons of such mothers. And they met [so the edition] the children of Israel coming out of Egypt with bread and water. So too those living well and in the catholic peace bestow the comfort of the word of God on those who, lately rescued from the bondage of sins through the water of baptism and the waves of the sea, pant for the liberty of the heavenly homeland. Which Berzellai the Galaadite did, who met David with his army fleeing from the face of Absalom with food, by which, refreshing them, he might make them stronger against the new tyranny; signifying those who strengthen the Church scattered by heretics with the aids of the heavenly word and encourage it to overthrow their madness. But while heretics strive to destroy the neophytes by their depravities and by the examples of others shown or by malignant words, as those born of incest they attack the people of Israel come out of Egypt with their arms, and with the counsels and wicked curses of Balaam, who is interpreted 'vanity of the people'; but God turned the curse of Balaam into a blessing of his people and defended it from the arms of the enemies.
19_interl239: because "to them that love God all things work together unto good"
19_interl240: concerning, namely, the two nations to be anathematized
19_marg296: AND IT CAME TO PASS etc. Because we must attend to the hearing of the truth, so that, when we are forbidden any one vice by the divine reading, we at once drive from our action and conscience whatever of defiling vice we detect in ourselves.
19_marg297: BUT IN ALL THIS etc. BEDE. This sentence, in which Nehemias says that he was not in Jerusalem, seems to belong not to the things which he had narrated above up to this point, but only to the present place. For the things above seem to have been done or said when the city was built, while Nehemias still stayed in Jerusalem. Which being vigorously completed, he returned to the king; in whose absence Eliasib made there a great storehouse in which should be laid up the things necessary either for the ministry of the house of the Lord or for the uses of the ministers; who also did not fear to place certain unlawful things in the storehouse and in the house of the Lord, which Nehemias on his return at once rooted out.
19_marg298: AND I CAST FORTH THE HOUSEHOLD STUFF etc. He who is mentioned above as the servant, the Ammonite, the enemy of the people of God; hence Eliasib did ill, who made a treasury for him, though his kinsman, in the porch of the house of the Lord, the vessels of the house of God and the other things which the use of the ministry required being cast out. "For what participation hath justice with injustice? What agreement hath the temple of God with idols?" What communion have heretics and schismatics with the orthodox and peaceable sons of God?
19_marg299: BEDE. Thou too, whatever of unbelief and uncleanness thou findest among the faithful, cast it out at once, that, the hearts of believers, which are the storehouses of the Lord, being cleansed, the vessels of the Lord may be brought in when they are full of the riches of the virtues; that is, that the hearts themselves, which a little before were vessels of error through fault, may become vessels of the Lord through correction; and there the sacrifice of good working and the incense of good prayer is made where before was a den of thieves.
19_marg300: They too cast the stuff of Tobias the Ammonite out of the storehouse of the temple and put back the vessels of the house of God and the incense who, heretics being excommunicated or false catholics expelled from the Church, put in their grades those who will serve Christ, who may serve him with faithful acts and prayers. This deed of Nehemias is indeed to be compared with the zeal of Christ, who, finding in the temple of God those who sold and bought, made a scourge of little cords and cast them all out. For as Nehemias represented his person in the other things, so also in this.
19_interl241: when it is necessary, namely, to provide the necessaries for this world
19_marg301: By the law we are commanded to work what is necessary for six days and to rest on the seventh, because all the elect in this world, which runs in six ages, ought to labour for eternal rest, but in the future day, as on the seventh, to hope for rest from the Lord. Tropologically, that is, morally, they keep the sabbath consecrated to the Lord when, separated for a time from the cares of this world, they give themselves to prayers and lift up a purified mind to the contemplation of heavenly things. For when we rightly do the things which the care of the flesh demands, we labour as it were on the six days at what is necessary. Since therefore we are occupied with those things which we need for this world, the sabbath-keeping of our prayers and devotion, in which we are free from temporal things that we may taste longer the joys of eternity, is rightly assigned to the seventh day, because it imitates the rest of the future life and of blessed praise. But foreigners seek to profane the sabbath day when earthly thoughts trouble us importunately in the time of prayer and draw us back from inner love by the memory or delight of temporal things. They lay on asses wine, grapes and figs and all manner of burdens and bring them into Jerusalem when, loading the foolish motions of the mind with carnal delights, they try to violate the rest of the heart dedicated to God. But Nehemias opposes these tumults of wicked thoughts, lest they disquiet our sabbath, when, with strict skill and the Lord's help, we shut out useless and foolish fancies from our heart in the time of prayer. For he charges them to sell such merchandise on a day on which it is lawful to sell when the soul devoted to God sets this measure to its thoughts: that in the time of prayer they abstain from the cares of passing things, yet at other times, when opportunity dictates, do not turn their regard altogether away from those things which belong to food and clothing, but dispense them with fitting moderation.
19_marg302: The good fish is pious faith; he who asks it of the Lord does not receive the serpent of unbelief. But the bad fish is the weak thought which plunges itself beyond measure into the cares of this world; which the Tyrians, that is, 'the distressed', seek to sell us on the sabbath when the unclean spirits importunately try to overwhelm the rest of our thought with the deep cares of the world. But for such trade Nehemias rebukes the nobles of Juda and chastises them, when the divine inspiration purges from such thoughts those who strive to serve the profession of piety.
19_marg303: Our conscience, if, purged from vices, it rejoices in God as its inhabitant, can be called Jerusalem; whose gates are the bodily senses, through which the things that are done outside come as it were by entering to the knowledge of our mind; which we are commanded to shut on the sabbath day, that, when we seek to give ourselves to God in psalms and prayers, we may drive from the mind whatever is done outwardly and with free mind pray to and praise the Judge alone in secret. And because no one becomes highest suddenly, but by long advance in holy living, while one [strives] to come, with grace as leader, to this perfection and peace of mind, it rightly follows therefore: I spoke also to the Levites etc.
19_marg304: Those must be purified from the daily exercise of work who desire to guard the gates of the senses from the assault of troubled thought.
19_marg305: He who desires to sanctify the sabbath day, that is, to make the leisure of prayer, psalmody, holy reading and tears profitable to himself, must have his conscience purified with much skill, that he may be able to accomplish the intention of good action. Which can also rightly be taken in the allegorical sense of the doctors of the faithful. For whoever long to guard the gates of the Church, namely the faith and works of their hearers, through which alone the Church is entered, from the contagion of heretics and of knocking vices, must first purify their mind and acts from every stain of errors.
19_marg306: In the Church they marry foreign wives who defile their conscience with the delights of crimes, which are properly the gentiles'; and the sons born of these cannot speak the Jews' language when the works which come forth from a vitiated mind show in themselves nothing of pious profession, but sound rather of gentile folly than of ecclesiastical chastity. For Azotus, which in Hebrew is called Esdod, [is interpreted] 'fire of words' or 'of breasts'. And therefore tropologically the sons of the foreign wives speak the speech of Azotus when the works begotten through wantonness await the vengeance of eternal burning. Hence rightly the begetters of such were not only rebuked and cursed by Nehemias, but some were also beaten; because it is necessary that those who err be more sharply restrained by the doctors of truth, that they may be carried over from the breast of the avenging fire to the breasts of divine praise. Heretics too, when they give their effort to the studies of gentile philosophy, dialectic and rhetoric more than to ecclesiastical simplicity, it is no wonder if their hearers speak according to the language of this people and that people, turning over the holy Scriptures with the mouth indeed, but interpreting them with gentile sense.
19_marg307: SO I CLEANSED etc. BEDE. An end open in all things and worthy of the building of the holy city and the temple of the Lord: that, the citizens being cleansed of pollution foreign to God, the courses of the priests and Levites be duly kept in their ministry, that the masters of the Church, established according to rule, may ever exhort the people, cleansed from all sin, to remain and grow in good for the rest.
19_marg308: Among other things the people offer wood to feed the fire of the altar when they work works of the virtues worthy of divine consecration. The wood burns and is consumed on the altar of holocausts when the works of justice are perfected in the hearts of the elect by the flame of charity.
19_marg309: Rightly does such a founder and dedicator of the city, after many labours of devotion, commend himself to the memory of the Creator and Giver of all good things.
19_marg310: BEDE. "And thou, supreme Father of lights, from whom every best gift and every perfect gift comes down, who hast given to me, the most humble of thy servants, both the love and the help of considering the wonderful things of thy law, and who hast granted to me, unworthy, the grace not only of embracing the old things in the treasury of the prophetic volume, but also of finding new gifts under the veil of the old and bringing them forth for the use of my fellow servants: remember me, my God, for good."
